This idea ties into the monsters wakening from a hibernation.

The madness starts in the countryside as people lose hope. As the despair spreads to the cities is becomes an epidemic. Citizens who helped their neighbor yesterday now hoard food and settle old debts. As the cycle feeds itself the fear and panic in the population spread at an ever increasing rate.

The old stories of the devastation, destruction, and chaos brought by the monsters is real. The stories, however, fail to mention the true cause of much of the loss, fear.

The players have made their way to a citadel or outpost to weather the coming storm. The population is starting to realize that their limited supplies cannot last more than a few months, and there are an ever increasing number of refugees. Slowly the safety of fortifications becomes a hive of danger and the once limitless storerooms begin to run dry.

Some of the refugees speak of punishment for sins, or the futility of hope. The troops no longer race to the defenses of the walls and patrols stop reaching the poorer sections of the camp. As the remnants of humanity tear themselves apart the party is one of the few beacons of hope. Their job is as much to rally the morale of the people as it is to defend the walls. Each loss they take, however, is felt twice as hard and each act of cowardice is magnified.

During one attack a wretched soul who has lost all hope opens a side gate in an attempt to flee and allows a small batch of the creatures into the poor section of the city. The resulting slaughter starts a riot...

Can the party help keep the citadel intact long enough for the monsters to retreat or aid to come? Will aid come?
Idea - As the bastion of humanity is under assault the citadel suffers a serious morale problem.
